body:
It seems that certain key modifiers does not work too(unless `KEY_MASK_CTRL` or `KEY_MASK_META` is part of the combination), for example:
- `KEY_MASK_SHIFT | KEY_A`
- `KEY_MASK_ALT | KEY_A`

After doing some research on Google, found [this post](https://developer.apple.com/forums//thread/763878?src=push&answerId=804374022#804374022) by an official Apple account on the Apple Developer Forums which states this is an intentional restriction in macOS 15, though I don't have an active copy of macOS 14 to test this against.

Apparently this is an anti-keylogger mechanism so that applications cannot capture inputs that would reasonably be considered as text rather than a shortcut. Originally it covered Option/Alt combinations too, but apparently that was rolled back according to [another post](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/763878?answerId=813718022#813718022) by the same account, though the implication is that Shift by itself still won't work. This doesn't seem to be well documented (I could only find this post, not something in the actual developed docs), so it may be worth documenting in Godot's docs.

I did find [this reference](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uikeycommand/wantspriorityoversystembehavior) for overriding system behaviour, but it only seems to apply to iOS and Catalyst-based apps. Using Accessibility Permissions/Input Monitoring is apparently one way around this, so that inputs can be picked up anywhere, but this would be an indirect solution,and Godot can already capture key events while focused regardless which it can then use internally, so it's unclear if there's much benefit to working around this.

> After doing some research on Google, found [this post](https://developer.apple.com/forums//thread/763878?src=push&answerId=804374022#804374022) by an official Apple account on the Apple Developer Forums which states this is an intentional restriction in macOS 15, though I don't have an active copy of macOS 14 to test this against.

This is for `RegisterEventHotkey`, it's not related to menus, but "text" shortcuts are likely consumed by root view (since it is implementing `NSTextInputClient`) and never get to the menu. Usually apps should not use shortcuts like this, so it still is a pretty reasonable limitation (we can forward events to the menu, but I'm not sure if this is a good idea).
